items.t: Airtel Payments Bank IPO in pipeline? Bharti Airtel payments business eyes D-Street debut, says report
sum: Airtel Payments Bank could become a much larger financial services business and may pursue an IPO in three to four years, Sunil Bharti Mittal said. The bank has nearly 100 million users and is targeting ₹10,000 crore in revenue and deposits, and ₹1,000 crore in profit.

Bharti Airtel’s financial services arm, Airtel Payments Bank, has the potential to emerge as a much larger financial services business, said Sunil Bharti Mittal, Chairman of Bharti Enterprises. He also indicated that Airtel Payments Bank could see potentially go public in next three to four years.
Airtel Payments Bank has the potential to get to ₹10,000 crore revenue, ₹1,000 crore profit, with a ₹10,000 crore deposit in the next few years, Mittal told CNBC TV 18 in an exclusive conversation.

Calling Airtel Payments Bank as a ‘sleeping giant’, Sunil Bharti Mittal, stated that there is a window for its IPO in the next three to four years, reported CNBC TV 18. He said that the company could attain a meaningful size after it achieves the target of ₹10,000 crores in deposit, ₹10,000 crores in revenue, and ₹1,000 crore in profit.

Airtel Payment Bank has a customer base of nearly 100 million users and it is inching closer to ₹4,000 crores in revenue. Its customer balance grew by 17% to ₹4,389 crore in the June quarter of financial year 2026-27 from ₹3,743 crore in the first quarter of last fiscal.
Its net profit increased to ₹19 crore in Q1FY27, which was 82% higher than the Q1FY26. The quarterly profit was driven by good operating performance.

The bank had earned a net profit of ₹10.4 crore in the April-June quarter of the previous financial year. Its net revenue surged to ₹831 crore from ₹777 crore in the corresponding quarter last financial year, Airtel Payments Bank said in a statement.

Bharti Airtel stock: Q2 growth lifts ARPU as costs weigh
sum: Bharti Airtel reported a mixed second-quarter performance on Friday, November 6, 2026, as higher revenue and profitability came with continued pressure on customer additions. The company discussed the results and its outlook in its Q2 FY27 earnings transcript.

Consolidated revenue reached INR 60,900 crore in the quarter, while EBITDAaL stood at INR 31,500 crore. Capital expenditure was INR 12,500 crore, leaving operating free cash flow above INR 19,000 crore, according to management.

Airtel said Africa delivered constant-currency revenue growth of 6.7 percent sequentially. India, excluding passive infrastructure, grew 3.2 percent sequentially, while the company continued to invest in cloud capacity and other growth businesses.

Mobile average revenue per user rose to INR 271 from INR 264. The company added 0.7 million revenue-earning customers and 2.9 million smartphone data customers during the quarter. Postpaid net additions reached 1.2 million, lifting postpaid customers to 8.3 percent of the total base.

Management said the latest prepaid pricing intervention had played out and identified plan upgrades, postpaid services, international roaming and top-ups as further ARPU levers. The comments point to a strategy focused on monetizing existing users rather than relying solely on subscriber growth.

Bharti Airtel is an India-based communications group serving customers across South Asia and Africa. Its portfolio includes mobile connectivity, 4G and 5G services, home broadband, digital television, payments, cloud, data centers, cybersecurity, Internet of Things and enterprise communications.

The company operates at large scale across India and Africa, with consumer and enterprise businesses supporting its diversification. In India, Reliance Jio is a principal telecom rival, while Airtel's African operations compete across multiple national markets with established regional operators.

Ex-Airtel COO Shares Years of Stress Led to Paralysis at 40
sum: RamG Vallath, former chief operating officer of Bharti Airtel, says years of high-pressure leadership roles contributed to a rare autoimmune disorder that left him effectively paralyzed by 40. He describes war rooms, missed targets and a seven-year wait for a diagnosis.

RamG Vallath, a former chief operating officer of Bharti Airtel, said in an interview published November 9, 2026 that years of high-pressure corporate work contributed to an autoimmune disorder that left him effectively paralyzed by age 40. The ex-Airtel COO shares years of detail on a career he says came at a steep personal cost.
Vallath, now 58 and an author, once dreamed of becoming a Fortune 500 CEO. He says the experience forced him to rethink what achievement means.

Vallath joined Titan in 1992 after management school. He described it as one of the lowest-paying recruiters on campus, but one with exceptional work-life balance. "I had a fantastic work-life balance," he said.
That changed as he rose through the ranks, first at Compaq and later in senior leadership roles at 3Com and Airtel.

The pressure began mounting while he was country leader at networking company 3Com. Weekly performance reviews turned into an intense exercise in accountability. "There was an immense amount of pressure," he said.
He recalled weekly meetings called "war rooms" where leaders had to explain sales funnels, missed targets and projections.

sum: Bharti Airtel on Thursday released its results for the second quarter of the ongoing financial year, reporting a 17% YoY increase in revenue from operations to Rs 60,878 crore, from Rs 52,145 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.

The telecom giant’s average revenue per user (ARPU), a key earnings metric for companies in the sector, rose to Rs 271 during the quarter from Rs 256 a year ago, maintaining its industry-leading position. Notably, peer and recently-listed Jio Platforms reported an ARPU of Rs 218.8 at the end of the September quarter.
Vodafone Idea is yet to announce its second-quarter earnings.
Also read | Bharti Airtel Q2 Results: Net profit jumps 31% YoY to Rs 8,887 crore; revenue up 17%; ARPU rises to Rs 271

Motilal Oswal shares that Bharti Airtel showed a good performance in Q2, largely driven by strong growth in Africa and robust wireless ARPU growth. After muted net additions in the first quarter, subscriber additions improved in homes, though ARPU decline accelerated. Further, the domestic brokerage noted that Bharti continues to trail Reliance Jio on HBB net additions.

Airtel Africa continued strong double-digit CC revenue and EBITDA growth, with further boost from cross-currency tailwinds. Reported capex rose 10% YoY, due to front-loading of capex in Africa. Bharti’s OCF generation remained healthy; however, recommencement of deferred 5G spectrum payments led to moderation in FCF to Rs 97 billion, Motilal noted. It has a ‘Buy’ call on the stock.

sum: Benchmark indexes rose in Japan and Australia, pushing the MSCI Asia Pacific Index up by 0.3%. That was after the S&P 500 Index jumped 1.6%, its biggest gain in three months, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 climbed 0.9%. South Korea was the outlier, with the Kospi Index dropping 2.7%, reflecting investor concerns over the future of data-center development and losses in US chip stocks.
Read more: Stocks in news: BSE, Lenskart, Nykaa, Bharti Airtel, LIC, Aurobindo Pharma and Nalco
Treasuries extended their gains from Wednesday on optimism lower oil prices will curb inflation. Bloomberg’s gauge of the dollar dropped for a second day.

US oil held its declines early Thursday after Brent crude slumped more than 8% to below $95 a barrel on Wednesday, following a pledge from Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer to end the Middle East war. Treasuries gained across the curve in US trading, as investors trimmed bets on Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes over the coming year. The dollar weakened the most in two months.

The equity market rally since the US election signals that investors are willing to look past a potential policy gridlock in Washington after Democrats wrested control of both chambers of the US Congress. The gain in Treasuries on oil’s slump and speculation that the so-called blue wave would limit President Donald Trump’s ability to add to the deficit is also seen as supporting stocks.

Since 1946, stocks have been higher one year after every midterm vote, including all four instances when both the House and Senate flipped to the party opposing the president, said Keith Lerner at Truist Advisory Services Inc.
“That supports our base case of giving the bull market the benefit of the doubt, but earnings, the economy, interest rates, valuations, and market trends remain more important to our view,” he added.

Massive surge! Reliance Industries shares up 12% after Q2; add ₹2 lakh cr in mcap — when did RIL last rally this much?
sum: The shares finished Monday’s trade with a solid 12% jump to settle at ₹1,300 on NSE, their highest level since early September. The stock last posted a comparable single-day surge in April 2020. Given its heavyweight status in the Nifty 50, the rally also lifted the index by 1.7%, even as tensions in West Asia remained elevated.

For long-term Reliance Industries shareholders, the sharp rise has revived confidence in the stock, which had been trending lower since the start of 2026. The shares closed in the red in eight of the previous 10 months. Despite Monday’s rebound, the stock remains down 17.22% so far this year.

The double-digit jump in the stock added ₹1.84 lakh crore to the company’s market capitalisation, taking it to ₹17.6 lakh crore and helping it retain its position as India’s most valuable listed company.

At its peak of ₹1,611, the company commanded a market capitalisation of ₹21.8 lakh crore. It had crossed the ₹21 lakh crore mark in June 2024, becoming the first Indian company to achieve this milestone.

Meanwhile, investors in the Reliance Group have another reason to celebrate, as its telecom arm, Jio Platforms, made a blockbuster stock market debut last week, listing at ₹1,440 apiece, a premium of 21.3% over its issue price.

Reliance Industries Ltd reported a record consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of ₹29,550 crore for the July-September quarter (Q2 FY27), marking a 33.8% increase from ₹22,092 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue rose 27.8% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹3,62,268 crore, while EBITDA increased 23.9% to a record ₹62,409 crore.

The strong performance was primarily driven by a recovery in the oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business, where EBITDA surged 67.9% to ₹25,203 crore, supported by higher global fuel margins and improved petrochemical spreads. O2C revenue increased 44.2% to ₹2,31,601 crore, with supply disruptions in West Asia and other regions pushing transportation fuel cracks higher.

Carlsberg India files updated IPO prospectus for 86.42 million shares
sum: This is the first public IPO prospectus from Carlsberg India, which had confidentially filed papers for the planned offering in July
Danish brewer Carlsberg's India unit moved closer to a public listing as it filed an updated draft prospectus for an initial public offering late on Tuesday.
The IPO is entirely an offer for sale of 86.42 million shares, the draft prospectus dated October 27 showed.

The move adds to a string of multinational companies turning to Indian equity markets to monetise their investments, rather than raise fresh capital. Hyundai Motor and LG Electronics have both pursued stake sales via Indian IPOs, attracted by relatively richer market valuations.
The potential listing would add to a busy period for India's IPO market, where large offerings from Jio Platforms and National Stock Exchange of India have shown strong investor appetite.

Carlsberg India operates through seven breweries it owns and nine third party manufacturers in India. It has a market share of 21.9% in 16 key states and union territories in Asia's third-largest economy, the updated prospectus showed.
The Indian unit's profit for the quarter ended June dropped 3.9% to 1.58 billion rupees ($16.61 million), while net revenue rose 21.5% to 13.66 billion rupees, as per the updated draft prospectus.

sum: The board recommended a final dividend of Rs 24 per fully paid-up equity share for FY26.

The revenue growth for the quarter was driven by sustained growth across India operations and a strong performance from Africa. India revenue, including passive infrastructure services, grew 8% YoY to Rs 39,566 crore. Africa delivered constant currency growth of 1.1% quarter-on-quarter.

Consolidated EBITDA increased 17% YoY to Rs 32,038 crore, while EBITDA margin expanded 60 basis points to 57.8%. India EBITDA stood at Rs 23,965 crore with margin improving to 60.6%. Consolidated EBIT rose 21% YoY to Rs 18,156 crore, with EBIT margin expanding 160 basis points to 32.8%.

The company said India's mobile revenue grew 8% YoY, aided by portfolio premiumisation and higher smartphone penetration. Airtel added 5.8 million smartphone users and 0.8 million postpaid customers during the quarter. Average revenue per user (ARPU) stood at Rs 257.

The company also announced several strategic initiatives during the quarter. Airtel partnered with Google to strengthen spam protection and Rich Communication Services messaging capabilities for users in India. It also launched the AI and Cyber Threat Research Center in collaboration with Zscaler to improve cyber resilience and accelerate trusted AI adoption in India.

During the quarter, Airtel unveiled expansion plans for its NBFC arm, Airtel Money Limited. The company said the subsidiary would be capitalised with Rs 20,000 crore over the next few years to scale digital lending operations. Airtel will contribute 70% of the planned capital infusion, while promoter group entity Bharti Enterprises will bring in the remaining 30%.
Capex for the quarter stood at Rs 16,066 crore as the telecom operator accelerated investments in 5G densification, fibre deployment, connected homes, data centres and enterprise services.

sum: The Sensex dropped around 1,313 points to close at 76,015, while the Nifty 50 fell 360 points to end the session at 23,816 on Monday. The selloff wiped out nearly Rs 6 lakh crore from the total market capitalisation of all companies listed on the BSE, bringing it down to Rs 467 lakh crore.

Titan shares crashed 7% to lead losses on Sensex, while the shares of IndiGo, SBI, Bharti Airtel, Eternal, Reliance Industries and NTPC followed, tumbling 2.5-5%. Bucking the trend, Sun Pharma and Hindustan Unilever shares gained around 1% each. Meanwhile, India VIX, which measures market volatility, surged more than 10% to 18.55

The bearish sentiment was broad-based, with the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 indices declining around 1% each. Nifty Consumer Durables and Nifty Realty crashed 4% and 3% respectively to lead losses among the sectoral indices. Around 2,366 stocks declined on NSE, while 963 advanced and 93 remained unchanged.

“The market will face pressure from two headwinds today. First, hopes of a resolution to the West Asia crisis have faded again following President Trump’s rejection of Iran’s proposal. Consequently, Brent crude has surged to $105, potentially aggravating the current account deficit. Second, PM Modi’s appeal to the nation to curb the consumption of petrol, diesel, gold, chemical fertilisers and edible oil, and to refrain from avoidable foreign travel, is a crisis-management response to the current account deficit problem caused by high crude prices. This call for austerity has slightly negative implications for economic growth in FY27,” said VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments.

US President Donald Trump on Sunday rejected Iran’s response to a US proposal for peace talks, dimming hopes for an end to the month-long conflict in the oil-rich Middle East. The conflict has caused widespread damage in Iran and Lebanon, disrupted maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and triggered a sharp rally in global energy prices.

Days after the US sent a peace proposal to Iran, Tehran responded on Sunday with conditions focused on ending the conflict across the region, particularly in Lebanon, where Israel is battling Iran-backed Hezbollah militants.

items.t: Bharti Airtel launches IQ Gateway: what it means for Bharti Airtel stock
sum: Bharti Airtel (INE397D01024) launched Airtel IQ Gateway on October 5, 2026, as a unified enterprise communications platform integrating SMS, voice, WhatsApp, RCS and number verification. Sahi reported that the platform is designed for secure customer engagement, fraud protection and lower delivery failures.

The launch extends Bharti Airtel's enterprise offering beyond connectivity into a single control system for messaging, voice and authentication. The platform uses network intelligence and Airtel IQ Verify to support silent SIM authentication, while trial deployments at banks and financial institutions preceded its nationwide rollout, according to ScanX News on October 5, 2026.

The commercial opportunity is already visible in Airtel Business. Revenue reached INR 5,665.4 crore in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, up 12.00 percent from INR 5,057.1 crore in the first quarter of fiscal 2026, while EBITDA rose 15.70 percent to INR 2,492.2 crore and the margin stood at 44.00 percent, Sahi reported on October 5, 2026.

Bharti Airtel's wider communications platform gives the new product a substantial distribution base. The company's investor-relations page says Airtel serves more than 650 million customers across 15 countries and operates mobile, home, digital television, cloud, cybersecurity and financial-services businesses.

The same company profile reports revenue of INR 1,729,852 million for the year ended March 31, 2025, compared with INR 1,499,824 million for the year ended March 31, 2024. EBITDA increased to INR 942,489 million from INR 790,458 million over the same periods, according to Bharti Airtel.

For investors, the next quantified checkpoint is the second-quarter 2026 report. TradingView lists November 5, 2026 as the next report date and shows consensus revenue of INR 598.17 billion and earnings per share of INR 15.09.

Ahead of that, the brokerage firm, Morgan Stanley, has shared its view on the telecom stock. The firm maintains an overweight rating with a latest target price. Here are the reasons why.
Morgan Stanley has reiterated its “Overweight” stance on Bharti Airtel, maintaining a target price of Rs 2,450, implying continued upside from current levels.
The brokerage highlighted that the recent AGR relief for Vodafone Idea was largely anticipated by the market and does not materially alter the broader industry outlook.
According to the firm, the structural “industry repair” thesis remains intact, even as discussions around a potential delay in tariff hikes persist.

items.t: Indian mobile giant Airtel raises $1 billion for data centers from Carlyle, other PE firms
sum: India's telecom giant Bharti Airtel has raised $1 billion for its data center arm — Nxtra Data — from private equity firms Alpha Wave, Carlyle and Anchorage Capital, underscoring a growing global interest in the sector.
Bharti Airtel is India's second-largest telecom operator and the raise will value Nxtra Data at about $3.1 billon once the transaction closes, the company said in a stock exchange filing on Monday.

Nxtra Data will receive $435 million from Florida-headquartered Alpha Wave Global, $240 million from existing investor Washington-based Carlyle, and $35 million from New York City's Anchorage Capital, Airtel said, adding that it will contribute the remaining amount.
The fresh capital will support Nxtra's expansion across India, Airtel said.
Gopal Vittal, executive vice chairman of Airtel, said Nxtra has built "data center networks" aimed at meeting the evolving needs of enterprises, hyperscalers, and government clients.

Nxtra has around 300MW of data center capacity, which will be scaled to 1GW "in the next few years, targeting ~25% market share," he added. It currently has 14 large data centers and more than 120 smaller, decentralized facilities located closer to end users and devices.

Data center demand globally has surged in recent years, largely driven by the explosion in AI workloads, which require vast computing power, electrical power, cooling and networking infrastructure. More than $61 billion flowed into the data center market in 2025.

sum: Earlier reports indicated that Singtel was set to offload about 0.8% of its stake in the Indian telecom operator.
The deal, estimated at around Rs 10,300 crore, was reportedly executed at a floor price of Rs 2,030 per share — a 3.1% discount to Airtel’s previous close.
The transaction is seen as part of Singtel’s broader restructuring strategy to optimize its holdings in regional telecom ventures.

Singtel has been progressively paring its stake in Bharti Airtel to unlock capital and refocus on core business areas. Earlier in May this year, the company sold a stake worth 2 billion Singapore dollars.

Additionally, Bharti Airtel reported a healthy consolidated free cash flow of Rs 14,600 crore. The company reaffirmed that its capital expenditure for FY26 in India, excluding investments in Indus Towers, is expected to decline from FY25 levels, a move likely to support better cash generation.

Looking ahead, analysts anticipate that Bharti’s premiumisation strategy and a probable tariff hike in December 2025 could contribute to significant improvements in revenue and free cash flows. Estimates project that the company may generate free cash flow of Rs 1 lakh crore between FY26 and FY27, according to research from Motilal Oswal.

Motilal Oswal has maintained a “Buy” rating on Bharti Airtel, with a revised target price of Rs 2,365. The brokerage noted consistent strength in both the Indian and African markets and forecasts Bharti’s revenue and EBITDA to grow at a compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) of 15% and 18%, respectively, over FY25–28. This growth is expected to be driven by tariff hikes, expansion in broadband services, and strong performance in the African segment.

sum: The floor price has been set at Rs 2,030 per share, representing a discount of about 3.1 per cent to Airtel's Thursday closing price of Rs 2,095

Pastel, a promoter group entity owned by Singapore’s Singtel, plans to sell shares of Bharti Airtel worth up to Rs 10,300 crore through block deals on Friday, according to the terms of the transaction.

items.t: Singtel sells about $1.2 billion stake in Indian telco Bharti Airtel
Singtel offers to sell stake worth $1.18 billion in India's Airtel, Bloomberg News reports
